title: Dropout: Randomly Dropping Units and Rescaling

paper.title: Improving neural networks by preventing co-adaptation of feature detectors

hook: During training, dropout randomly removes units from a layer. But at test time, all units are present. How do we keep the expected output the same?

symbols.meaning: Vector of activations from the previous layer.
Weight matrix connecting previous layer to current layer.
Bias vector of the current layer.
Binary mask vector: 1 means keep the unit, 0 means drop it.
Output of the layer after applying dropout and rescaling.
Probability of keeping a unit (1 - dropout rate).

equation.caption: Dropout applied to a layer's pre-activation, followed by rescaling by 1/p.

explorations.title: Effect of keep probability on rescaling
explorations.predict: If we decrease p (more dropout), what happens to the rescale factor 1/p and the output for kept units?
explorations.observe: With p=0.5, the rescale factor is 2. Each output y_i = z_i * 2 = 2. The sum of outputs is 8, while the sum of pre-activations is 4.
explorations.why: The rescale factor 1/p compensates for the fact that only a fraction p of units are kept on average. Without rescaling, the expected sum of outputs would be p times the sum of pre-activations.

explorations.title: Dropped units contribute zero
explorations.predict: If a unit is dropped (mask=0), what is its output?
explorations.observe: Unit 1 has mask=0, so its output y_1 = 0. Units 2-4 have mask=1, so their outputs are z_i / p = 1/0.8 = 1.25.
explorations.why: The mask multiplies the pre-activation, so a dropped unit's contribution is zero. The rescaling only applies to kept units.

self_tests.name: No dropout (p=1) leaves output unchanged
self_tests.expect: approx(out.y[0], inp.z[0], 1e-6) && approx(out.y[1], inp.z[1], 1e-6) && approx(out.y[2], inp.z[2], 1e-6) && approx(out.y[3], inp.z[3], 1e-6)

limitation: This toy model assumes a fixed mask and does not simulate the randomness of dropout during training. It also ignores that dropout is typically applied to hidden layers and that the rescaling is an approximation to maintain expected output.
misconception: Dropout does not simply remove units; it also rescales the remaining outputs so that the expected sum of activations remains the same as without dropout.

claims.text: Dropout randomly drops units with probability 1-p during training.
At test time, weights are scaled by p (or equivalently, activations are scaled by 1/p during training).
In our toy setup, we apply dropout to a fixed pre-activation vector and rescale by 1/p to illustrate the effect.

outcomes.outcome: Explain how dropout randomly drops units and why outputs are rescaled.
Compute the output of a layer with dropout and rescaling given pre-activations, mask, and keep probability.
Understand that the expected output of a unit under dropout equals its pre-activation when rescaling is applied.
